carryIn: startHex is ignored by the product; mapRadius >= 7 is needed; initiative is random so the acting principal is read from the history (A2FP facts, census.md section 5).

DISCRIMINATION (new): the product reads the FIRST sideAssignments entry of a side as its owner (MatchWireSealedChoices.ts:86-89). A stale assignment appended AFTER the real owner (the #2318 draft did this) never wins that lookup, so the stale rows would not fail even with the spectator guard (line 77) deleted. prepare therefore puts the stale assignment FIRST for the ACTIVE side and refuses unless staleEffective is true.

ROLE POLICY: gm only when meta.coopCampaign.campaignId is set AND an active campaign_session_participant row (campaign_id, session_id, participant_id, seat gm) exists (MatchSeatMembershipSource.ts:105-124). The row lives in the SQLiteService DB; the harness points DATABASE_PATH and MULTIPLAYER_DB_PATH at the same file and server.js:463-464 runs SQLiteService.initialize(), so migration 17 creates the table on first boot (unverified on a built image; ready/prepare refuse with "participant table missing" otherwise).

PRODUCTION GM SEAT: co-op creation seats the GM host as a spectator-kind seat (src/pages/api/multiplayer/matches/index.ts:172-178). The GM-branded spectator rows are the real GM configuration; the non-spectating (human-seated) GM is a policy probe.

The fixture-only co-op marker disables the foreign-unit guard (ServerMatchHostIntent.ts:566) and is read by CampaignHostRegistry.createEntry (CampaignHostRegistry.ts:442-475) only on campaign-sync sockets, which no A2 leaf opens; the tactical recovery path does not read it (rg coopCampaign src/lib/multiplayer/server shows no MatchHostRegistry/recovery reader).
Capability tables are not in the match file: DurableMatchStore.ts:614-620.

The F closure receipt must check the offline op sequence of its own run in evidence.jsonl (the three A2FP rows contribute ready,declared,ready,declared,ready,ready,declared; the trusted rows add their prepare and ready/declared calls) and the F runner must not skip a witness call by design.

The F run restarts the server more often than A2FP (8 matches); a failure limited to that probe timeout may be re-run once with both runs disclosed; any other failure, or a second probe timeout, stops for Root.
